## [2026-09-03] Individual Meritocratic Belief: hard-work item missing from 1999 — H1/H3 restricted to 2009/2019
**Context:**  Extracted the actual ZA8790 "Variable Report" codebook
(`data/codebooks/ISSP/cumulation/ZA8790_cdb.pdf`) directly. 
**What went wrong:** the Methodology Outline state the hard-work item (MAIN Individual Meritocratic Belief measure) is "available and coded consistently in all three waves" (1999/2009/2019).
The codebook shows this is false: the item (`v6` in the cumulation) is
explicitly marked "Variable not available in this module" for ISSP 1999 —
it only exists in 1987, 1992, 2009, and 2019. Cross-checked directly against
the 1999 questionnaire PDF (`ZA3430_bq.pdf`): the 1999 "getting ahead"
battery asked about wealthy family and knowing the right people only, not
hard work. Same problem, worse, for the ambition item (`v4`, the two-item
robustness measure's second component): available only in 1987/1992/2009 —
missing from BOTH 1999 and 2019, not just 2019 as previously assumed.
**Decision:** H1 and H3 (both use `ind_belief_c` as a moderator) are
restricted to the 2009 and 2019 waves only. 1999 is dropped from these two
models explicitly, not left in and relying on implicit listwise deletion — the sample restriction should be stated plainly in the methods/results write-up, not
buried. The two-item robustness check (hard work + ambition) is now a single-wave (2009-only) check, not a 1999/2009 comparison — `wave` was dropped from that model's formula since it would otherwise be a constant with no variation.
H2 alone (credential × stratification, no belief term) doesn't strictly need
this restriction, but the current script tests H1/H2/H3 jointly in one
three-way-interaction model, so the restriction applies to the whole main
model as specified. Splitting H2 out into its own three-wave model is a
possible follow-up but wasn't decided here.
**Why this matters:** this shrinks the effective sample for the chapter's
two central, novel hypotheses (H1, H3) by a full wave and needs a
limitations-section footnote.  It also means "the Chapter 1 sample" now
means different things depending on which hypothesis is being reported
(27-country/3-wave for descriptives and H2 alone if split out later;
27-country/2-wave for H1/H3 as specified).


## [2026-10-26] Rebuild from scratch: recodes verified against codebook labels
**Context:** Rebuilding the pipeline in a new repo (`CH1_recognition_injury`) with minimal packages.
**Decision:** Every recode (`sss`, `credential`, `ind_belief`, `income`, `gender`, `age`) was checked
against the value labels and with old-vs-new cross-tabs before use. Negative codes (-9/-8/-7/-3/-1) → `NA`.
`ind_belief` = 6 − `v6` (5 = strongest hard-work endorsement). Stratification direction checked
(Austria/Germany/Hungary = 8; Australia/Canada/NZ/USA = 0).

## [2026-10-27] ISEI missing for ~19.5% of respondents
**What I found:** Almost all are ISCO-88 missing codes (mainly -4: respondents with no job),
not lookup gaps; code 110 (armed forces, 482 cases) is the only real unmatched code.
**Decision:** Left as `NA`. Non-working respondents drop out of any model with occupational status;
this goes in the attrition table.

## [2026-10-27] Tertiary enrolment (WDI) missing for six sample country-waves
**What I found:** Australia, Germany, Japan, New Zealand, Portugal and the USA have no
`SE.TER.ENRR` value for 2006–2012 in the download, so none for the 2009 wave. This is why
the old main model had 25 countries (Portugal drops out entirely; Canada has only 1999).
**Decision:** Baseline keeps `tertiary` as `NA` (no interpolation). Five countries enter the main
model with 2019 only. Planned sensitivity check: refit without `tertiary` as a control.

## [2026-10-27] Respondents aged 15–17 kept
**Decision:** Only `AGE = -9` set to `NA`. 455 respondents aged 15–17 and one aged 105 are
retained. Restricting to 18+ is a possible sensitivity check.
